gen-righteous-general-sans: General Sans reads smooth and steady, its tall lowercase filling the line with no snags at the curves. And Righteous, bent from thin steel rod, gives that easy flow a commanding, playful lid.
gen-tourney-manrope: Tourney stretches its words with wide tracking and bulky, oversized small letters. Manrope's bright, open curve mouths soften the heavy heading, and that friendliness is what holds the pair together.
gen-audiowide-fs-paquito: Paquito reads confident and friendly, with capitals sitting barely above its lowercase and low stroke contrast. And Audiowide, tile-like and uniform in stroke, adds a tech edge while the text beneath reads easily.
gen-dafont-aaargh-fs-neco: A blunt, commanding shout of uniform strokes, that's Aaargh. Neco adds the gentle swell of a barely pressed round brush, giving that shouting heading a dignified, measured partner below.
gen-dafont-ozone-fs-paquito: Paquito comes in confident and friendly, with a low-contrast serif build. Ozone's geometric forms barely lift capitals above lowercase, and Paquito's own minimal step lets the two line up smoothly.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-fs-merriweather: Wobbly, nearly sealed letters make Jelly Crazies feel playful. Merriweather Sans opens its e clearly to the right, and its tall lowercase keeps words looking sturdy and large, so reading moves steadily.
gen-dafont-redux-fs-merriweather-sans: Contemporary and geometric, Redux spreads wide letter spacing and generous entries into every curve. Merriweather Sans grounds that with large, sturdy-looking words and an e whose eye opens clearly rightward.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-archivo: Heavy and stencil-cut, Plakkaat keeps its letters closed up tight. Archivo's curves open outward, backed by a commanding x-height, and that closed-versus-open tension is what makes the pair work.
gen-dafont-stencilia-satoshi: Structural and striking, Stencilia leaves spacious gaps at its curve ends. Satoshi keeps a constant stroke width beneath a soaring x-height, and that steadiness is the pair's main pull.
gen-gf-autour-one-switzer: Switzer draws tubular, wire-like letters with a tall waist line and c tips that never drift toward touching. Autour One then adds bold, expressive channels into every round letter.
